I couldn't do this research. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed with a "no more tool calls remaining" error, so I couldn't open any page: not Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit, Barnes), NET Bible notes or any of the others.

Your rules say to report only what the pages I read actually say, cite a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. With nothing read, I have no notes I can give you. Writing commentary on Job 33 from memory and attaching URLs would break those rules and could give you sources that don't say what I claimed.

**Planned research for a new session:**

1. **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
   - enduringword.com/bible-commentary/job-33/
   - biblehub.com/commentaries/[ellicott | gill | pulpit | barnes]/job/33.htm
   - preceptaustin.org
2. **Differences between traditions.** The likeliest place is vv. 23–24, the "messenger… mediator… I have found his ransom" passage. The question is whether it points to Christ, an angel or a human teacher. I'd look at Gill, the Wesley notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon sermons and Reformed sources. Other candidates are:
   - v. 4 (the Spirit of God as Creator)
   - vv. 14–18 (God speaking through dreams, which matters for Pentecostal and charismatic views on continuing revelation, e.g. samstorms.org)
   - vv. 19–22 (illness as God's discipline)
3. **Other views:**
   - NET Bible translator notes, especially on "messenger/mediator" and "ransom"
   - bibleodyssey.org on Elihu's place in the book
   - Catholic and Orthodox readings: Gregory the Great's *Moralia on Job* (ccel.org) and Aquinas's commentary on Job
   - Pages on these sites about whether Elihu's link between suffering and sin supports prosperity or word-of-faith ideas

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll work through these sources and write the verse-by-verse notes with a URL for each point.
